Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

We’re looking for a Financial Analyst, GTM to serve as the primary finance partner to our Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role sitting right at the center of GTM decisions, helping leadership decide where to invest, improve productivity, and drive predictable ARR growth.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

 - Location: Remote-first (United States; BC & ON, Canada)

 - Full-time

 - Permanent 

 - Exemption status: Exempt (US Only) 

 - The cash compensation for this role is tailored to align with the cost of labor in different geographic markets. We've structured the base pay ranges for this role into zones for our geographic markets, and the specific base pay within the range will be determined by the candidate’s geographic location, job-related experience, knowledge, qualifications, and skills.
   
   - United States (all figures cited below are in USD and pertain to workers in the United States)
     
     - Zone A: $112,000 - $135,000
     
     - Zone B: $105,000 - $126,000
     
     - Zone C: $98,300 - $118,000
   
   - Canada (figures cited below are in CAD and pertain to workers in ON & BC, Canada)
     
     - $123,000 - $147,000

This role is also eligible to participate in Webflow's company-wide bonus program. Target amounts are a percentage of base salary and vary by career level. Payouts are based on company performance against established financial and operational goals.



Please visit our Careers page https://webflow.com/careers#pay-zones for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

 - Application Information:
   
   - Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
   
   - This posting is for an existing vacancy

 - Reporting to the Director of Corporate Finance
   
   

As a Financial Analyst, GTM, you’ll:

 - Own the GTM expense plan and forecast, covering headcount and non-headcount spend, and turn it into executive-ready commentary for Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leaders on variances, risks, and investment tradeoffs

 - Manage GTM headcount planning and capacity, including hiring plans, ratios such as quota-carrying reps to sales support, and attrition, and flag drift from targets before it affects the forecast

 - Reduce manual effort in planning by improving Workday and Adaptive Planning workflows, removing manual tagging, and setting materiality thresholds so non-headcount forecast updates focus on spend that moves the outlook

 - Own the single source of truth for ARR and ATR across our Sales and Self-Serve models, auditing the ARR in Salesforce and the data warehouse, documenting metric definitions, and resolving breaks with Revenue Operations, Data and/or Accounting

 - Run the monthly churn, renewal, and write-off review with GTM partners, preparing the analysis, root-cause commentary, and forecast implications leaders use to make decisions

 - Synthesize multi-source data from Salesforce, the data warehouse, Workday, and NetSuite into clear metrics, KPIs, and business narratives that inform GTM leadership decisions

 - Build working relationships across Finance, Accounting, Procurement, and GTM to drive alignment without formal authority, and automate recurring reporting with SQL, spreadsheets, and AI tools





ABOUT YOU:

Requirements:

 - BS / BA college degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field, or relevant experience

 - 3+ years of experience in FP&A, corporate finance, investment banking, consulting, or public accounting; experience in SaaS or a subscription business is preferred

 - Strong proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets, including building models from raw data



You’ll thrive as a Financial Analyst, GTM if you:

 - Have a working understanding of SaaS metrics such as ARR, NRR, GRR, churn, and renewals, and can trace them back to source data in Salesforce and the data warehouse

 - Enjoy partnering with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leaders and can explain financial results in plain terms to non-finance audiences

 - Notice manual work and fix it, whether with SQL, spreadsheet automation, or AI tools

 - Bring accounting fluency, including accruals and the monthly close; a CPA and a Big 4 background is preferred

 - Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

 Why Join EDC?

 Work-Life Balance : EDC offers a competitive compensation package & work-life balance. We have hybrid work options, 3 to 4 weeks paid vacation, a corporate closure period, summer early Friday’s.

 Team Overview 
 The Sectors and International Advisory (SIA) Team helps Canadian companies grow internationally by combining sector expertise, actionable market intelligence, strategic advice, and connections to global business opportunities. The team develops and delivers EDC’s prioritized sector strategies and works across EDC to translate knowledge of Canadian capabilities, global value chains, and market needs into practical choices and opportunities for exporters. 
 As Manager, Sector Research, you will lead and develop a team responsible for research on Canadian business ecosystems, industry sectors and subsectors, and global value chains. 
 This is a player/coach role: you will set priorities, create the conditions for strong team performance, and remain directly involved in high-value research, analysis, and the development of executive-ready insights and recommendations. 
 You will bring sound judgement, curiosity, and an experimentation mindset to complex research questions. You will coach researchers, establish clear research standards and reusable ways of working, and collaborate with various internal teams. You will ensure researchers identify the appropriate stakeholders for each assignment and recognize when collaboration or a hand-off to another team for deeper research or specialized support may be appropriate. Your work will help EDC identify where Canadian capabilities align with international demand and where EDC can have the greatest impact. This role will report to the Vice President, Sectors and International Advisory.

 Lead, coach, and develop a team of researchers by setting clear outcomes, assigning work thoughtfully, providing timely feedback, supporting professional growth, and fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and accountable team environment.

 Remain a hands-on researcher by leading selected high-priority studies on firms, Canadian sector and subsector ecosystems, competitive dynamics, technologies, and domestic and global value chains. 
 Investigate complex business and sector issues, select fit-for-purpose qualitative and quantitative methods, and integrate primary research, secondary sources, firm-level data, financial information, and market intelligence. 
 Establish and uphold standards for research quality, source integrity, analytical rigour, responsible use of AI-enabled tools, peer review, documentation, and clear communication of assumptions and limitations. 
 Translate complex evidence into practical sector strategies, opportunity assessments, company and ecosystem profiles, briefings, presentations, and recommendations that support prioritization and decision-making. 
 Connect Canadian capabilities to international demand by helping to identify gaps, , supply-chain opportunities, and areas where EDC’s insights, advisory services, market-development capabilities, connections, and financial solutions can advance exporter growth. 
 Build trusted relationships across EDC and with external experts, industry associations, government partners, companies, and research organizations to test hypotheses, broaden evidence, and increase the reach and usefulness of insights. 
 Create reusable tools, datasets, playbooks, and knowledge-sharing practices that improve team productivity, strengthen institutional knowledge, and make insights accessible to non-expert audiences. 
 Monitor delivery, research impact, stakeholder needs, and emerging trends; adjust priorities as evidence changes and communicate progress, risks, and recommendations to senior leaders.

 Completed degree in Economics, Political Science, Business Administration, International Business, Data or Social Sciences, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. 
 Minimum ten years of progressive experience in market or sector research, economic or industry analysis, business strategy, consulting, international trade, or a related field, including experience leading complex work and guiding others.

 A strong record as a hands-on researcher who can personally structure and execute complex assignments while overseeing a broader portfolio and enabling others to deliver.

 Advanced strategic-research and consulting-style analytical capabilities, including framing complex business and sector issues, developing hypotheses, integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence, and producing decision-useful recommendations. 
 Experience with primary and secondary research, company profiling, firm-level datasets, market sizing, competitive analysis, and relevant commercial trade, market, and industry-intelligence platforms. 
 Strong knowledge of Canadian sector and subsector ecosystems, exporter capabilities, innovation systems, and international supply chains, with the judgement to distinguish evidence from inference. 
 Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing requests, manage projects and resources, improve processes, and deliver high-quality work in a changing environment. 
 Ability to build trust, collaborate across disciplines, and influence senior leaders and partners without relying on formal authority. 
 Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills in English, including the ability to explain complex findings clearly, concisely, and credibly to executive and non-expert audiences. 
 Advanced proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, collaboration tools, and AI-enabled research tools such as Copilot, combined with sound judgement regarding validation, confidentiality, and responsible use.

 Bilingual in both official languages (French and English). 
 Experience leading a research, intelligence, economics, strategy, or advisory team in a matrixed organization. 
 Experience with data visualization software such as Power BI or Tableau to communicate complex findings to non-expert audiences. 
 Experience in financial analysis, including interpreting financial statements, evaluating company performance, assessing industry financial trends, and integrating financial insights with market and sector research. 
 Experience in one or more of EDC’s strategic sectors, such as Agri-Food, Advanced Manufacturing, Digital Industries, Defence & Security, Energy & Energy Transition, or Critical Minerals.

We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment that respects people from all cultures, backgrounds, and abilities. Group Ventures is Valsoft's incubator. We find opportunities in the market and build companies to address them. The finance team inside Group Ventures keeps the books for four of those companies so far: ValPay, Tenerum, Sadie Technology, and Plug & Pay.
 We're looking for a financial analyst to run their day-to-day accounting cycle: vendors, payments, banking operations, recurring schedules, and close support. You'll work directly with the Finance Controller, who keeps responsibility for accounting judgement, financial statements, and technical positions. You'll be the one running the accounting engine each day.
 The work spans several entities and seven currencies (CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CHF) on NetSuite OneWorld. Volume is high and close deadlines are tight.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to draft, analyse, and automate the repetitive parts of the cycle. You're responsible for the accuracy of whatever gets posted.
 What we value 
 Accuracy, and the habit of checking your own work before anyone else has to.
 Finishing what you own without being chased.
 Understanding how each entity earns and spends money.
 Discretion with confidential financial information.
 Curiosity, and a willingness to fix a process that keeps producing the same error.
 The honesty to say when something is wrong, including your own work.
 What you'll do 
 Keep payables accurate and vendors paid on time
 Monitor the AP shared mailboxes (ValPay, Tenerum, Sadie) and run the weekly invoice-entry batch: triage, rename and file PDFs, code invoices by entity, division and GL account, prepare the NetSuite bill import file, and attach supporting documents. Process recurring invoices per established coding rules.
 Obtain missing spend approvals from budget owners, reconcile vendor statements, investigate differences, and clear past-due invoices.
 Set up and maintain vendor records in NetSuite, including banking details, tax forms and payment terms, checking every banking change before it goes in.
 Prepare the weekly payment run: payment proposal, draft-only payment entry in the banking portal, remittance advices, and approval follow-up.
 Keep cash and bank records reconciled
 Download bank statements and transactions for all entities, code and post entries in NetSuite, and prepare the monthly bank reconciliations with reconciling items listed for review.
 Own the credit card cycle: collect receipts, chase cardholders, produce the monthly expense file, and prepare the reconciliation and journal-entry upload file.
 Get customers invoiced and cash applied
 Issue and send customer invoices, and follow up on missing or corrected ones.
 Apply cash receipts, maintain the AR aging, and handle first-level collection follow-up, flagging past-due accounts and disputes to the Controller for escalation.
 Support the month-end close
 Maintain recurring schedules (prepaids, accruals, fixed assets and depreciation, deferred revenue) and prepare balance sheet reconciliations for lower-complexity accounts, documenting open items.
 Prepare standard and recurring journal entries with full supporting documentation for Controller review and approval, then upload the approved files to NetSuite and verify posting accuracy.
 Run intercompany confirmations: prepare balance confirmations, circulate them to group entities, follow up, and assemble settlement support.
 Keep records audit-ready and support the Controller
 File and archive supporting documentation per the established folder structure, pull samples and documents requested by external auditors, and keep audit folders current.
 Handle finance requests in Jira, gathering documentation, keeping tickets updated and closing them once resolved. Write and maintain the procedures for the tasks you own.
 Work with the Controller on ad hoc requests and special projects: onboarding new entities or acquisitions, opening and closing bank accounts, system implementations, and data gathering for analyses and reporting. Prepare the documents, data extracts and working files for files the Controller leads, and pick up other accounting-cycle work as team needs and period priorities change.
 What you'll bring 
 A DEC in accounting and management techniques, an AEC in accounting, or equivalent training.
 Two to four years of full-cycle accounting experience.
 Intermediate to advanced Excel. You're comfortable with lookups, pivot tables, and high volumes of data.
 ERP experience. NetSuite is strongly preferred; Sage, Dynamics, or QuickBooks are accepted.
 Accuracy and attention to detail, with the discipline to meet tight close deadlines.
 Self-direction and organisation. You can carry a high volume of recurring tasks with minimal supervision.
 Follow-through. You chase the missing approval, receipt, or confirmation until it arrives.
 Discretion and judgement with confidential financial information.
 Clear writing. You can explain a reconciling item or a vendor discrepancy in a few lines.
 You use AI tools in your work and check the results before they reach the ledger.
 Useful experience 
 Multi-entity or multi-currency accounting.
 Power Query.
 Payments, fintech, or software.
 Using a corporate banking portal.
 Jira.
 Writing procedures for a finance team that is still being built.
 Who will enjoy this role 
 You notice when a vendor statement doesn't match, a bank line has no home, or an intercompany balance is off by the same amount two months running. You want to know why, and you fix the cause.
 In one week you might clear an invoice batch across three entities, chase a cardholder for receipts, reconcile an AUD bank account, and pull audit samples. Most of the work recurs, and the value is in getting it right every time.
 The hard parts are specific. Volume is high and the close date doesn't move. Across seven currencies and several entities, small mistakes compound. You prepare and the Controller decides: accounting judgement and final approvals sit with someone else. Processes are being built as the team grows, so sometimes you'll do a task that has no procedure yet, then write one.
 Why this role matters 
 Group Ventures builds companies for Valsoft, and its growth has been recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50. ValPay operates as a payment facilitator, so other businesses can accept payments without building their own merchant infrastructure. Sadie builds AI voice technology for restaurants and hospitality, with customers in Australia, Europe, the United States, and Canada.
 Each new company the group builds becomes another entity in the finance team's books, with its own bank accounts, vendors, and close. The team is small and still being built out. This hire takes on the day-to-day accounting cycle so the Controller can focus on accounting judgement, financial statements, and technical positions. You'll see how a multi-entity, multi-currency technology group runs from the inside, and as the team scales there is room to take on more analytical work.

 Casual | Employee or Independent Contractor | Flexible Scheduling | Central East Region 
 The Care Company is a home healthcare organization dedicated to creating A Better Life for Those at Home . We support clients of all ages to live safely, independently, and with dignity in the comfort of their own homes. Our mission is to help people Make Each Day Count by delivering exceptional, person-centred care that puts people first and strives to be Better Today than we were yesterday.
 We are seeking a passionate and experienced Occupational Therapist (OT) to join our community rehabilitation team. This role is ideal for an OT who enjoys the autonomy of managing their own community caseload while being supported by an experienced interdisciplinary team.
 This is a flexible, casual opportunity that can be structured as either an employee or independent contractor position , depending on the successful candidate’s preference. Whether you are looking to supplement an existing caseload, build your community practice, transition into community care, or simply enjoy the flexibility of accepting referrals that fit your schedule, we would love to hear from you.
 You will work closely with clients and their families in the home, completing comprehensive assessments, developing individualized treatment plans, and recommending equipment and environmental modifications that promote safety, independence, and quality of life. Many of the individuals we support are living with complex or chronic medical conditions and require Alternate Level of Care (ALC) services.
 This is an exciting opportunity to join The Care Company as we continue to build and expand our Occupational Therapy program . We are looking for therapists with an entrepreneurial mindset who are excited to help shape the future of community rehabilitation. Beyond delivering exceptional clinical care, there will be opportunities to contribute to new service development, Requests for Proposals (RFPs), quality improvement initiatives, and innovative models of care that can help expand Occupational Therapy services across the community.
 As our OT program continues to evolve, there will also be mentorship and leadership opportunities for therapists interested in helping shape the future of community Occupational Therapy. This includes opportunities to mentor Occupational Therapy students during community placements, support the development of future clinicians, assist with onboarding new therapists, and contribute to clinical resources and best practices.
 Who This Role Is Perfect For 
 This opportunity may be a great fit if you are:
 An Occupational Therapist looking to supplement your existing caseload or practice.
 Interested in working as either an employee or independent contractor.
 Looking for greater flexibility and autonomy over your schedule.
 Passionate about helping clients remain safe and independent in their homes.
 Interested in mentorship, leadership, and supporting future Occupational Therapists.
 Entrepreneurial-minded and excited by the opportunity to help build and grow an evolving community rehabilitation program.
 Comfortable working independently while knowing clinical and operational support is available when needed.
 What You’ll Do 
 As an Occupational Therapist with The Care Company, you will have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in clients’ lives while enjoying the autonomy and flexibility of community practice. Working collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team, you will:
 Complete comprehensive in-home assessments within the required referral timeframe, including functional assessments, mobility evaluations, falls risk assessments, equipment needs, and ADL/IADL evaluations.
 Develop individualized, evidence-based treatment plans that empower clients to maximize independence, safety, and quality of life in their own homes.
 Provide follow-up visits focused on functional goal progression, mobility, environmental modifications, home safety, cognitive and physical strategies, and caregiver education.
 Recommend, trial, and prescribe assistive devices, adaptive equipment, and home modifications, collaborating with vendors and contractors where required.
 Support clients and families through education, coaching, and practical strategies that promote confidence, independence, and successful aging in place.
 Collaborate closely with nurses, physiotherapists, Personal Support Workers, physicians, care coordinators, case managers, and Ontario Health atHome to support seamless care transitions.
 Coordinate equipment procurement and assist with ordering supplies through Ontario Health atHome vendors.
 Monitor client outcomes and modify treatment plans as clinically appropriate to support meaningful, measurable progress.
 Maintain accurate, timely, and clinically sound documentation.
 Communicate proactively with the office regarding caseload availability, scheduling changes, and urgent referral readiness.
 Independently manage your caseload and schedule while receiving administrative, scheduling, clinical, and technical support from The Care Company.
 Deliver compassionate, ethical, and evidence-informed care while upholding The Care Company’s commitment to clinical excellence.
 Beyond Clinical Care 
 This role offers more than a traditional community caseload. As The Care Company continues to expand its Occupational Therapy services, you may also have opportunities to:
 Help shape and grow our community Occupational Therapy program.
 Contribute to new service development and Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
 Participate in quality improvement and innovative models of community care.
 Mentor Occupational Therapy students during community placements and help develop the next generation of OTs.
 Support the onboarding and mentorship of future Occupational Therapists joining the organization.
 Collaborate with leadership on the development of clinical resources, processes, and best practices.
 Grow into future clinical leadership and mentorship opportunities as our rehabilitation program expands.
 Scheduling 
 Flexible, casual scheduling with no fixed weekly schedule.
 Accept referrals based on your availability and geographic preference.
 Initial in-person home assessments are generally expected within 48–72 hours of receiving a visit request within your geographic service area.
 Ability to independently manage scheduling and communicate promptly with the office regarding availability.

 Travel between client homes is required; access to a reliable vehicle is considered an asset.
 Qualifications and Experience 
 Registered and in good standing with the College of Occupational Therapists of Ontario (COTO) .
 Experience providing home and community care, particularly with HCCSS and/or Ontario Health atHome clients , is strongly preferred.
 Community Occupational Therapy experience and/or hospital discharge and transition-planning experience will also be considered.
 Demonstrated skill in functional assessments, equipment recommendations, safety evaluations, ADL/IADL retraining, and caregiver education in the home environment.
 Experience with equipment and supply ordering through Ontario Health atHome vendors is an asset.

 Ability to work independently in the community and produce clear, timely, clinically appropriate documentation.

 Compensation

 $25 per 30 minutes of approved administrative time completed outside of scheduled client visits, including documentation, care coordination, report writing, supply ordering, funding applications, and other client-related administrative duties.
 Why Join The Care Company?

 Autonomy to build and manage your own community caseload while being supported by an experienced interdisciplinary team.

 Help build something meaningful – play an active role in shaping and expanding The Care Company’s Occupational Therapy program.
 Opportunities to contribute to RFPs, new programs, quality improvement initiatives, and innovative models of community rehabilitation .
 Mentorship opportunities with Occupational Therapy students and future clinicians.
 Opportunities for future clinical leadership and program development.
 24/7 clinical support from experienced clinical leadership whenever guidance is needed.

The Director will provide direction and implement strategies to support the foundational pillars of the university’s mission to advance research funding.

Canadian Tri-Agency (NSERC, SSHRC and CIHR) activities are of vital importance. Not only do these agencies fund research directly but they drive other factors: partnership programs to attract industry funding; set quotas for certain programs (Canada Foundation for Innovation, Canada Research Chairs, equipment grants, undergraduate research awards, and some graduate awards); and determine the Research Support Fund allocation.  The Director will be responsible for a significant portfolio of sponsors, setting strategic priorities within the unit and supervising professional staff.

Procurify is looking for a motivated, collaborative, and creative person who is passionate about technology.



Procurify is the AI-enhanced procurement and AP automation platform for mid-market organizations. We make it easy for organizations to take control of spend and save money. 



We're looking for a pragmatic and thoughtful engineering leader to help scale our platform, development practices, and team.

You’re a person with a knack for solving some of the most pressing technology challenges in SaaS application development while levelling up the team of engineers around you, and you’re eager to help our customers achieve the best version of themselves.



Everyone at Procurify is a team player. A big part of this role involves a desire for personal growth, and a customer-centric mindset. We’re seeking entrepreneurial people who are willing to challenge the status quo and contribute to larger strategic objectives.




WHAT YOU’LL BE WORKING ON:



 - Build & Ship End-to-End Features: Design, develop, and maintain full stack features—from RESTful APIs and backend services to responsive, user-friendly frontend components—using Python/Django and TypeScript/React.

 - Develop Scalable Backend Services: Build and evolve backend systems that handle business logic, data storage, and integrations, ensuring performance, reliability, and scalability.

 - Create High-Quality Frontend Experiences: Implement reusable, accessible, and performant UI components in React. Collaborate with product and design to deliver intuitive user experiences.

 - Design & Optimize Database Schemas: Contribute to the design of our database models and write efficient, secure queries. You will work to ensure the performance and integrity of our data layer.

 - Strengthen System Architecture: Provide leadership in the technical output of your team and ensure technical designs follow appropriate design patterns, are architecturally sound, and adhere to secure coding practices.

 - Ensure System Reliability: Enable the observability and monitoring of relevant system behavior in the areas of the application owned by your team and use the data collected to propose improvements to application performance and stability.

 - Our Tech Stack:
   
   - Application: Python/Django, Typescript/React
   
   - Cloud: AWS
   
   - Infrastructure & Containers: AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform
   
   - Databases: MySQL
   
   - CI/CD: CircleCI




WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR:



 - Full Stack Experience: 5+ years of professional experience in hands-on work across both frontend and backend systems, preferably in a SaaS environment.

 - AI & ML: Deep understanding of LLMs, prompt engineering, RAG architectures, vector databases (Databricks/pgVector), and agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, Google ADK, or similar)

 - Python Proficiency: Strong experience building and maintaining applications using Python and a major web framework (we use Django).

 - React: Experience building modern web applications with React and TypeScript, including component-based architecture and state management.

 - Agile & Collaborative: Experience working with agile practices (Scrum/Kanban) and CI/CD principles. You thrive in a team environment.

 - Empathetic & Accountable: You act with compassion, believe that your team’s success is your success, and communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical colleagues.

 - Maintains a professional and current LinkedIn profile, ensuring it is updated upon joining Procurify to reflect their new role and maintain a consistent company presence.




LEAD WITH CARES:



 - Commitment: Demonstrates accountability and follow-through, delivering reliably and owning outcomes in a way that others can depend on.

 - Ambition: Takes initiative with curiosity and a growth mindset, pursuing bold ideas that elevate impact and performance.

 - Resilience: Shows adaptability, composure, and perseverance through challenges, staying focused and effective in a fast-changing environment.

 - Excellence: Brings rigor, collaboration, and a strong quality focus to deliver high-performing solutions and raise the bar for outcomes.

 - Simplicity: Applies focus, clarity, and streamlining to cut through complexity and enable efficient, impactful execution.




WHAT MAKES PROCURIFY A GREAT PLACE TO WORK FOR ENGINEERS:



 - A modern tech stack with opportunities to influence future architecture.

 - A culture committed to learning, experimentation, and engineering excellence.

 - Clear technical vision and empowered teams who own their outcomes.

 - Genuine collaboration, psychological safety, and a people-first culture.

 - Meaningful problems to solve with real customer and business impact.

WE’RE COMMITTED TO HELPING MISSION-DRIVEN ORGANIZATIONS SPEND SMARTER

Procurify is a remote-first company with a big heart and a strong ambition to modernize the way organizations manage business spend. The short version
 Every order Portless ships moves money in two directions. We bill merchants for shipping, fulfillment, storage, duties and taxes, and we pay carriers, warehouses and partners across several countries and currencies. Our P&L sits in the middle.
 We've grown fast, and we're investing in the systems behind that money flow to match. We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own it end to end: from rate card to invoice to cash, and from carrier bill to audited cost.
 About Portless
 Portless is changing the face of global e-commerce. By decoupling brands from traditional, expensive domestic warehousing, we let e-commerce companies ship directly from manufacturing hubs to global consumers in as little as three to five days.
 We move packages to 75+ countries for hundreds of DTC brands, with millions of packages shipped annually, 99.8% pick-and-pack accuracy, and 98% on-time delivery. We're a small, remote-first team growing fast, and the work you do here shows up in a merchant's business, and on our own books, within weeks.
 What you'll own
 We're building out our finance infrastructure for the next stage of growth. You'll set the product direction for:
 Billing (order to cash). Rate cards, pricing rules, invoicing, disputes and collections. You'll own our billing engine from the product side, including rolling it out across our merchant base.
 Cost audit (procure to pay). Ingesting carrier and partner invoices, matching them to what we shipped, and catching discrepancies automatically.
 Margin visibility. A shipment-level view of revenue, cost and pass-through charges that finance and leadership can rely on.
 Duties and taxes. How tariffs, VAT and other pass-through charges are calculated, billed and collected, in close partnership with our compliance team.
 The merchant experience. How merchants see, understand and ask questions about their charges.
 You'll be the bridge between finance, operations and engineering, turning finance needs into a clear roadmap.
 What success looks like
 First 90 days
 An end-to-end view of how money moves through Portless today, and a clear picture of where it needs to go
 A finance product strategy and sequenced roadmap, aligned with finance, operations and engineering
 Priorities set and defended in writing, with the reasoning and tradeoffs behind them
 First 6 months
 Most merchants billed automatically and on time
 Our largest carriers' invoices matched and audited automatically
 Finance can see margin by shipment, merchant and lane
 Measurable time given back to the finance and CS teams

 Product craft first. This is the bar we're least flexible on.
 5+ years in product management owning a complex, data-heavy domain
 You can map a messy process to where data originates, where it breaks, and where the leverage is
 You get your own answers with SQL or AI tools, and check claims against what actually happened
 You ship what works this quarter while building toward the right end state, and you write it up clearly
 Finance and logistics experience.
 You've built product for billing, AP, carrier audit, payments or financial infrastructure, ideally in logistics, freight or fulfillment
 You're fluent in rate cards, accruals, pass-through vs. revenue, invoice matching, and how operational data reaches the GL
 You work closely with accountants and finance ops and know when to bring in the CFO. This isn't an accounting role
 Exposure to duties, tariffs or VAT is a strong plus
 How you work.
 Forward-deployed: close to finance, our China operations and merchants, with evening calls and potential travel to China

Reporting to the Vice President, Talent, Transformation & Design, the incumbent owns the enterprise change method, demand prioritization, adoption readiness and executive-level visibility of change saturation. The mandate is to identify, plan, sequence and land change with the business, making adoption an engineered outcome rather than a communications task applied at go-live.  

The Core Responsibilities: Enterprise Change Enablement Strategy 
 Establish and maintain the enterprise Change Enablement practice within People & Talent, including standards, methods, tools, intake, demand prioritization and governance routines. 
 Own a tiered support model that sizes change enablement effort based on employee impact, adoption risk, complexity and strategic importance. 
 Maintain enterprise visibility of change saturation across major transformation programs and provide clear recommendations on sequencing, readiness and trade-offs.

 Design leader and manager enablement approaches that equip people leaders to communicate change with clarity, handle difficult questions and reinforce desired behaviours. 
 Create and maintain reusable change playbooks, templates, communications inputs, training supports and adoption measurement practices that can be scaled across initiatives. 
 Use employee feedback, pulse checks, readiness data, service data and adoption telemetry to identify friction early and adjust enablement plans. 
 Ensure change enablement aligns with EQB’s culture refresh, ways of working and employee experience commitments so transformation lands in a credible and consistent way. 
 Portfolio, Measurement and Executive Reporting

 Partner with Finance value tracking teams to connect adoption and readiness to benefit realization, while maintaining clear accountability boundaries. 
 Partner with Risk, Compliance and control functions to ensure change plans meet regulatory expectations and produce evidence of readiness, adoption and sustainment where required.

 CO280 is a leading developer of low-carbon industrial infrastructure projects. We've identified and pre-qualified more than 20 industrial sites representing approximately 6 GW of potential capacity — not just parcels of land, but strategic infrastructure platforms with existing industrial zoning, water rights, transmission access, and established host relationships that dramatically compress development timelines in a market where speed-to-power is everything. 
 This is the rare moment when a market this large is gated by a problem this specific. The AI buildout is the defining industrial expansion of the decade, and power is the constraint holding it back, with interconnection queues running four to seven years and the industry defaulting to unabated gas it does not want to burn. CO280 is building the platform that answers it.  
 You'll join a close-knit team of entrepreneurial, collaborative, and transparent operators who have developed, delivered, and scaled new technologies and industrial infrastructure across multiple verticals.  We believe clean power must be practical, bankable, and scalable to move the needle on net zero and earn social license. If you want to help build the projects the energy transition is waiting on, this is a seat at the table.

 The Vice President Project Development will build and lead CO280's low carbon power data center infrastructure platform — owning project origination, development strategy, strategic partnerships, and the project development organization. You will identify, originate, secure, and advance gigawatt-scale infrastructure opportunities from concept through Final Investment Decision (FID), working across utilities, industrial hosts, OEMs, EPCs, hyperscalers, AI developers, and capital partners to turn strategic sites into bankable projects. 
 This is a relationship-driven leadership role. Success will depend as much on the executive relationships you bring as the projects you've delivered. Existing relationships across hyperscalers, neoclouds, data center developers, utilities, power developers, OEMs, EPCs, infrastructure investors, and other strategic partners will enable CO280 to originate opportunities faster and build projects that competitors cannot.

 This role exists because the AI industry has discovered that compute is no longer constrained by chips — it's constrained by power. Every major hyperscaler is competing to secure gigawatts of generation capacity while utilities face interconnection queues measured in years. CO280 is uniquely positioned to solve that problem by combining strategic industrial sites, deep customer relationships, and proven infrastructure development expertise. The Vice President Project Development will convert those advantages into one of North America's largest low-carbon infrastructure portfolios.

 Building CO280's project development function and playbook.

 Securing the company's first anchor AI infrastructure customers. 
 Advancing the first one or two projects to Final Investment Decision.

Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 - Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 - Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 - Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 - Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 - Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.
   
   - Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.
   
   - Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.
   
   - Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 - Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

ValPay is one of the fastest-growing companies in Canada.
 Our growth has been recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50, and we've reached a turning point.  ABOUT THE ROLE 
 This role is a rare chance to help build a finance function where accounting and technology meet. Our finance setup dates from our startup days, and we're rebuilding it to match the pace and complexity of the business.
 As Senior Controller, you'll own revenue recognition and technical accounting across multiple entities. Just as important, you'll have real, hands-on ownership of the automation and data work that more and more of our finance function runs on.
 This role is ideal for a CPA who's ready to grow beyond traditional accounting and specialize in accounting and technology together. You don't need deep AI or automation experience. What matters most is a strong accounting foundation and the drive to build that expertise.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
 Own revenue recognition and every judgmental or complex accounting entry across all entities, including usage-based and payfac revenue under IFRS
 Review and approve accounting entries across the group
 Set technical accounting policy for the group, and make sure it's applied consistently across entities in different jurisdictions
 Own and keep improving the group's core processes and controls across multiple entities and currencies, and build scalable, well-documented processes as we grow
 Lead the multi-entity close and consolidation
 Take a hands-on role in building the automation and data infrastructure that connects usage, billing and payment-settlement data across the group. As the function matures, you'll have a real chance to build deep expertise in financial systems and data modeling.
 Build your skills with AI tools in day-to-day work such as journal entry review, reconciliation and reporting, with the goal of making them central to how you work
 Manage and review the work of the Controller and transactional support staff, bringing organization, structure and focus to a team we're building from the ground up
 Be the main escalation point for technical accounting questions, taking over this role from the CFO
 Work directly with our international tax specialist and external auditors on statutory filings, transfer pricing and audit requirements across our four entities
 WHAT YOU'LL BRING 
 CPA designation (or equivalent international designation)
 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of technical accounting
 Solid understanding of IFRS
 Experience closing and consolidating financials across multiple legal entities and/or jurisdictions
 Experience reviewing and managing the work of other accounting staff, either as a people leader or through strong review and mentoring

 French proficiency (our team is based in Montreal)
